issues.title: Tracking Issue for "C-unwind ABI", RFC 2945
issues.body:
<!--
Thank you for creating a tracking issue! 📜 Tracking issues are for tracking a
feature from implementation to stabilisation. Make sure to include the relevant
RFC for the feature if it has one. Otherwise provide a short summary of the
feature and link any relevant PRs or issues, and remove any sections that are
not relevant to the feature.

Remember to add team labels to the tracking issue.
For a language team feature, this would e.g., be `T-lang`.
Such a feature should also be labeled with e.g., `F-c_unwind`.
This label is used to associate issues (e.g., bugs and design questions) to the feature.
-->

This is a tracking issue for the RFC "C-unwind ABI" (rust-lang/rfcs#2945).

The feature gate for the issue is `#![feature(c_unwind)]`.

This RFC was created as part of the ffi-unwind project group tracked at https://github.com/rust-lang/lang-team/issues/19.

### About tracking issues

Tracking issues are used to record the overall progress of implementation.
They are also uses as hubs connecting to other relevant issues, e.g., bugs or open design questions.
A tracking issue is however *not* meant for large scale discussion, questions, or bug reports about a feature.
Instead, open a dedicated issue for the specific matter and add the relevant feature gate label.

### Steps
<!--
Include each step required to complete the feature. Typically this is a PR
implementing a feature, followed by a PR that stabilises the feature. However
for larger features an implementation could be broken up into multiple PRs.
-->

- [ ] Implement the RFC
- [ ] Adjust behavior of panic `extern "C" fn"`
  - https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/issues/123231
  - https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/129582
- [ ] Adjust documentation
  - https://github.com/rust-lang/reference/pull/1226
- [ ] Stabilization PR ([see instructions on rustc-dev-guide][stabilization-guide])

[stabilization-guide]: https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/stabilization_guide.html#stabilization-pr
[doc-guide]: https://rustc-dev-guide.rust-lang.org/stabilization_guide.html#documentation-prs

### Implementation notes

Major provisions in the RFC:

* [x] Add a `C-unwind` ABI and `system-unwind` (I think), we may need more variants.
* [ ] For external functions with the C ABI, we already (I believe) add the "nounwind" LLVM attributes when we build them. We want to continue doing this.
* [ ] For external functions with the C-unwind ABI, we do *not* want any such attributes.
* [ ] For Rust functions defined with the C ABI, e.g., `extern "C" fn foo() { ... }`, we want to force them to abort if there is a panic. The MIR helper function [`should_abort_on_panic`](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/nightly-rustc/rustc_mir_build/build/fn.should_abort_on_panic.html) already exists and I think will modify the generated code to insert the required shims in such a case. They should also be marked as "nounwind" in LLVM, if they're not already. 
* [ ] Rust functions with the "C-unwind" ABI should **not** abort on panic.
* [ ] Use ABI to guide the "nounwind" attribute on callsites as well.
* [ ] Write suitable codegen tests to check generated LLVM IR.

### Unresolved Questions
<!--
Include any open questions that need to be answered before the feature can be
stabilised.
-->

None. The unresolved questions in the RFC were meant to be solved by future RFCs building on this one.

### Implementation history
* Initial implementation: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/76570
* Additional work (removing `#[unwind]`, adjusting panic handling): https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/86155

issues.title: `c_unwind` full stabilization request: change in `extern "C"` behavior
issues.body:
Tracking issue: #74990

This is a separate issue to enable using the FCP bot a second time. The request-for-stabilization comment is duplicated below, without modification.

RFC "C-unwind ABI": https://github.com/rust-lang/rfcs/pull/2945

Feature gate to be stabilized: `#![feature(c_unwind)]`

Stabilization PR: https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/116088

classification.name: AbortUnwindingCalls
evidence: The PR stabilizes `c_unwind` and changes `layout::fn_can_unwind` so C-family ABIs are classified solely by their `unwind` flag. `AbortUnwindingCalls` is the concrete MirPass that consumes this helper for both the body ABI and call sites, so the PR changes its terminate/cleanup decisions. The edited `ffi_unwind_calls.rs` provides queries/lints, not a separate MirPass.

analysis.originalLogic: Before this PR, `layout::fn_can_unwind` classified the C-family ABIs (`C`, `System`, `Cdecl`, `Stdcall`, `Fastcall`, `Vectorcall`, `Thiscall`, `Aapcs`, `Win64`, `SysV64`) as may-unwind using `unwind || (!tcx.features().c_unwind && tcx.sess.panic_strategy() == PanicStrategy::Unwind)`. Thus, on stable (feature disabled) with `panic=unwind`, even a plain `extern "C"` was reported as may-unwind. The stabilization changes this to classify those ABIs solely by their `unwind` flag, so plain `extern "C"` is nounwind and only `extern "C-unwind"` (and other `*-unwind` ABIs) may unwind. `AbortUnwindingCalls` consumes this helper for both the body ABI and call sites. The PR also removes the extra `abi_can_unwind` workaround from `has_ffi_unwind_calls`.
analysis.incorrectTransformation: Historical pre-stabilization behavior: for a plain `extern "C"` body or call compiled with `panic=unwind` and without the `c_unwind` feature, `fn_can_unwind` returned true. Consequently `AbortUnwindingCalls` treated the boundary as may-unwind and left the unwind path intact instead of replacing it with a terminate/abort action. This conflicted with the plain C ABI's nounwind contract and with LLVM's historical `nounwind` marking, so an unwind could escape a plain `extern "C"` boundary. The corrected invariant after stabilization is: plain C-family ABIs never unwind, so unwinds crossing them must terminate/abort; `extern "C-unwind"` remains may-unwind and must not be forcibly aborted at that boundary.
analysis.inputDomain: Rust MIR functions and calls whose ABI is a C-family ABI, with and without the `-unwind` suffix, under `panic=unwind` and `panic=abort`, and with/without the historical `#![feature(c_unwind)]` gate. Relevant constructs include Rust-defined `extern "C"` / `extern "C-unwind"` functions that panic, calls to imported C-family functions, inline asm marked as may-unwind, and `catch_unwind`/FFI unwind diagnostics.
analysis.summary: Stabilizing `c_unwind` changed the ABI-unwind classification consumed by `AbortUnwindingCalls`: on stable `panic=unwind`, plain C-family ABIs were previously over-approximated as may-unwind via a feature-gated panic-strategy check; after the PR only the ABI's `unwind` flag matters. This makes plain `extern "C"` nounwind and forces unwinds crossing it to terminate, while `extern "C-unwind"` still permits propagation. The accompanying `abi_can_unwind` workaround in `ffi_unwind_calls` is removed because the helper no longer over-approximates.
analysis.trigger: A Rust function or call uses a plain C-family ABI (e.g. `extern "C"`) and an unwind attempts to cross that boundary while compiling with `panic=unwind`. Under the old feature-gated logic the boundary was treated as may-unwind, so the abort/terminate decision for the unwind edge was wrong. The same trigger with `extern "C-unwind"` must continue to allow unwinding.
preconditions: The callee or body ABI is a C-family ABI; only the `unwind` flag distinguishes plain ABI from `*-unwind`.
The compile uses `panic=unwind` for the historical behavior change to be observable; `panic=abort` does not exercise the removed feature-gated fallback.
The historical incorrect behavior required the `c_unwind` feature to be disabled (stable mode).
The function body or call can actually unwind (for example it panics or resumes an unwind).
The `AbortUnwindingCalls` pass uses `fn_can_unwind` for both body ABI and call-site ABI decisions.
pitfalls: Do not conflate `fn_can_unwind` (may-unwind classification) with the removed `abi_can_unwind` workaround (ABI's unwind flag only); the old `has_ffi_unwind_calls` deliberately ANDed both.
Do not drop the extra `abi_can_unwind` conjunct while `fn_can_unwind` still over-approximates plain C, or the ffi-unwind query behavior changes independently of the pass fix.

Do not treat a retained test name or old comment as proof that an old abort/no-abort decision is still correct; the deleted `nounwind-on-stable-panic-unwind.rs` explicitly documented the old behavior.
Do not assume `extern "C"` and `extern "C-unwind"` are interchangeable in may-unwind tests; the patch updates panicking asm test helpers from `extern "C"` to `extern "C-unwind"`.
Several assembly/codegen tests gained `-C panic=abort` because a plain C ABI can no longer unwind; absence of that flag changes test expectations.
`panic=abort` cases are not a substitute for testing `panic=unwind`, where the old feature-gated fallback applied.
analysis.testStrategy: Construct two otherwise identical programs that differ only in the ABI suffix on a panicking Rust function and/or an imported panicking callee: plain `extern "C"` versus `extern "C-unwind"`, compiled with `-C panic=unwind`. For plain C, verify the unwind is terminated/aborted at the boundary (inspect MIR unwind action and/or generated LLVM `nounwind` attributes); for C-unwind, verify the panic can propagate and is not forcibly aborted. Also compile the plain-C case with `-C panic=abort` as a control. Use codegen tests under `tests/codegen/unwind-abis` that check generated LLVM attributes, plus run/UI tests such as `tests/ui/panics/panic-in-ffi.rs`; update may-unwind tests to use `extern "C-unwind"` for functions that must actually unwind. The patch's deleted `tests/codegen/unwind-abis/nounwind-on-stable-panic-unwind.rs` is the regression test for the old wrong expectation.
